answer: Give each account its own coding task every epoch, drawn by public beacon from a large bank and scored by hidden unit tests instead of peer votes. Like a falcon that must make every dive itself, each fake must solve a different problem, so N accounts cost N real solutions, and one shared solution fails the other tasks' tests. Passed tasks stay on record as a relic of proven work that weights later pay, and the next horizon of tasks stays unseen until the epoch opens.
